name: Texture Flow
description: Tracks oriented texture element propagation across frames using structure tensor analysis to detect flow discontinuities where AI generators fail to maintain spatiotemporal texture coherence.
mechanism:
This method analyzes texture flow patterns in video for deepfake detection:

1. **Texture Flow Estimation**: The motion field of texture elements (rather than edge features) is estimated using oriented texture correlation between frames. This captures how textured regions (skin, hair, fabric) move over time.

2. **Texture-Motion Consistency**: Texture flow should be consistent with optical flow — texture moves with the surface it belongs to. The method compares texture flow with geometric optical flow (from edge features). Inconsistencies indicate texture that moves independently of the underlying geometry — a possible AI generation artifact.

3. **Surface-Texture Coherence**: As surfaces rotate, textures foreshorten according to perspective. The method checks whether texture deformation is consistent with the estimated surface orientation change. Deepfake face generators may rotate faces without properly foreshortening skin texture.

4. **Texture Temporal Stability**: Fixed textures (skin pores, wrinkles, fabric pattern) should maintain their spatial relationship to surface geometry across frames. The method tracks texture-surface binding — texture that "slides" relative to the surface (like a projection rather than a surface property) indicates AI rendering.

5. **Texture Flow Boundaries**: Texture flow should be continuous within objects and show discontinuities only at object boundaries (depth edges, occlusion boundaries). The method detects texture flow discontinuities within surfaces — internal flow breaks corresponding to face-swap boundaries reveal the extent of generated regions.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through texture flow analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
